content_voiceover: This slide covers the checkpoint inhibitor data in relapsed refractory Hodgkin lymphoma. The biologic rationale is genetic: classical Hodgkin lymphoma frequently carries amplification of chromosome nine, p, twenty four, which co-amplifies the PD-1 ligand genes and JAK2. Increased JAK2 signaling further upregulates PD-1 ligand expression, driving both immune evasion and increased proliferation of the malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg cells, which is why PD-1 blockade works so well in this disease. Nivolumab, studied in patients who had failed both autologous transplant and brentuximab vedotin, achieved an overall response rate of sixty six point three percent. The most common grade three to four adverse events were neutropenia and lipase elevation, each around five percent, with pyrexia being the most common severe adverse event; nivolumab received F-D-A approval on this basis. Pembrolizumab, studied in the KEYNOTE-zero-eight-seven trial in the same relapsed refractory population, achieved a similar overall response rate of sixty nine percent, with fatigue as the main adverse event, and was likewise F-D-A approved. Together these trials made PD-1 inhibitors a standard option for Hodgkin lymphoma relapsing after transplant and brentuximab.
keypoints: 9p24 amplification co-amplifies PD-1 ligand genes and JAK2, driving immune evasion and proliferation
Nivolumab: ORR 66.3% in post-ASCT, post-BV relapsed HL; grade 3-4 neutropenia and lipase rise (~5% each); FDA approved
Pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-087): ORR 69%, mainly fatigue; FDA approved
Both PD-1 inhibitors are standard salvage after ASCT and brentuximab vedotin failure
keypoint_voiceover: The key biology is nine p twenty four amplification, which co-amplifies PD-1 ligand and JAK2, giving Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg cells a built-in immune escape mechanism, and that is exactly why PD-1 blockade works so well here. Nivolumab and pembrolizumab both showed response rates in the mid to high sixty percent range in patients who had already failed autologous transplant and brentuximab vedotin, and both are F-D-A approved in that setting. Know the toxicity signatures: neutropenia and lipase elevation for nivolumab, fatigue for pembrolizumab.
